title: Instrument Panel Speaker Removal and Refit — Vehicles With SYNC
introduction: The instrument panel speaker sits beneath the grille near the windshield, with the center finish panel coming off first for access. I think of this as opening a small cupboard: releasing the front panel does not mean everything behind it is free. The optional ICM connection and the speaker harness attachments need attention before the parts can come away. This guide covers the supplied removal and refitting sequence for vehicles with SYNC; it does not diagnose an audio complaint.

requirements.category: Match the documented audio interface before starting

items.name: Non-touchscreen SYNC controls
items.detail: Before dismantling anything, confirm that the fitted non-touchscreen SYNC radio has the VOL/Power knob, RADIO button, TUNE knob and Seek controls described in the completion check. If the fitted system differs, stop before dismantling and obtain its matching owner operating instructions and applicable repair procedure. This article verifies the documented interface, not every SYNC variant.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to take these precautions may cause serious personal injury. Review the applicable warnings in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before beginning.

items.name: Trim access
items.detail: Use an Interior Trim Remover for the instrument panel trim and center finish panel, as specified in [Instrument Panel Center Finish Panel](#/document/G1693976).

items.name: Speaker fasteners
items.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and torque equipment for the speaker-bolt tightening value given beside the electrical-disconnection instruction.

items.name: Optional ICM
items.detail: The supporting center finish panel illustration shows an optional ICM. Disconnect and reconnect its rear electrical connector only if that equipment is fitted.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal instructions before starting; they also include details needed when installing the speaker.
edits.why: The speaker-bolt tightening value is included with removal, even though it is used during refitting.

edits.text: Remove the instrument panel center finish panel to gain access to the speaker grille. Refer to: [Instrument Panel Center Finish Panel](#/document/G1693976) (501-12 Instrument Panel and Console, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: First use the Interior Trim Remover to release the clips on the narrow RH instrument panel trim strip immediately outboard of the glovebox, then remove that strip. Next release the center finish panel’s clips around the vent/gauge area and across the passenger-side fascia, using the trim remover, and move the panel clear of its mountings. If the optional ICM is fitted, reach the electrical connector at the rear of the panel and withdraw its plug from the ICM socket before taking the panel away. In the supporting rear view, the plug withdraws toward the right; this direction describes the back of the panel, not the view from the seat. The connector’s latch mechanism is not specified.

edits.text: Lift the instrument panel speaker grille upward from its exposed front edge and remove it.
edits.why: The upward arrow identifies the grille’s removal movement. With the finish panel already removed, the grille can come off to expose the speaker beneath it.

edits.text: Remove the speaker mounting bolts and lift the instrument panel speaker clear of its mounting position, allowing access to its wiring. Disconnect and detach the wiring as described below before taking the speaker away.
edits.why: The magenta mounting bolts secure the blue speaker assembly. Lifting it from its mounting position provides access to the rear connector; the harness still needs to be freed.

edits.text: Detach the speaker harness at the attachment beneath the rectangular component and at the separate attachment beside the upright harness run. Disconnect the electrical connector at the rear of the speaker by withdrawing its plug from the socket, then remove the speaker. During installation, tighten the speaker mounting bolts to Torque: 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).
edits.why: The main drawing marks both harness attachment locations, while the inset shows the speaker plug withdrawing from its socket. These are separate releases: unplugging the speaker alone does not free the retained harness. The tightening value applies to the speaker bolts, not to the connector.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order. Reconnect the speaker plug to its rear socket, refit the harness attachment beneath the rectangular component and the separate attachment beside the upright harness run, then seat the speaker and tighten its mounting bolts to the value given above. Refit the speaker grille. If the optional ICM is fitted, insert its electrical plug back into the socket on the rear of the center finish panel before seating that panel. Engage the center finish panel clips, then refit the RH trim strip beside the glovebox and engage its clips.
edits.why:
I account for the wiring attachments before closing the trim, just as I would check a cupboard for a trapped cord before shutting the door. Confirm that the speaker connector, both harness attachments and any fitted ICM connector have been restored, and that the grille and trim clips are engaged.

After all wiring and trim are restored, keep the car parked in P for an automatic or a parked gear for a manual, with the parking brake applied, wheels chocked and the engine stopped. With the valid key inside, start from ignition OFF and press the start button without pressing either pedal to switch the ignition ON without starting the engine. For the documented non-touchscreen SYNC radio, if the audio is OFF, press the VOL/Power knob to turn it ON; if it has already resumed ON, leave it ON rather than toggling it. Press RADIO to select the radio band, then turn TUNE or press Seek to find a familiar station. Turn VOL to a comfortable level and listen for sound from the replaced speaker. This is an ordinary function check, not fault isolation. After the check, press VOL/Power to turn the audio off, then press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to return the known ON state to OFF. Remove the key. If the sound is absent or abnormal, keep that OFF/key-out state before reopening trim or checking a connector. The keyless controls and audio interface are described in the supplied Ford Mustang owner’s manual.
